basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 2.' and it opens 'Vers. 2. Inirent bellum contra Bara. Bara malitia vel creatura interpretatur. Est rex'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 2. Inirent bellum contra Bara. Bara malitia vel creatura interpretatur. Est rex Sodomorum, id est pecudis silentis. Bersa interpretatur in angustia, est rex Gomorrhae quae interpretatur populus | timens. Sennaar [Vulg., Sennaab ] interpretatur excussio vel fetor dentium, et est proprium nomen hominis. Est rex Adamae, quae interpretatur terrena. Semeber ibi perditio interpretatur. Est rex Sebon quae interpretatur vinculum moeroris. Bale civitatula interpretatur vorago vel praecipitatio. Vocatur etiam vitula consternans. Ferunt enim Hebraei hanc tertio terrae motu corruisse. Ipsa est Senor id est parvula.
